title: Seeing Beyond the Next Step: World-Model-Guided Human-Like Navigation in Multi-Agent Scenes
abstract: arXiv:2611.07730v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Selecting a next motion in a populated scene is not just a matter of avoiding what is currently in the way: an action can be locally feasible yet drift onto the road instead of the crosswalk, cut into a stream of crossing pedestrians, or bottleneck a narrow passage. These failure modes are invisible from the current state alone, and acting on them requires reasoning about what each candidate action will cause. World models offer exactly this, namely action-conditioned predictions of the future, but rolling them out at every decision step is a cost deployable navigation systems cannot pay, and the field has largely traded foresight for speed. We argue this is a false dichotomy. The natural place for a world model in human-aware navigation is at training time, as a preference oracle that distills foresight into a fast policy, rather than at inference time, as an online planner. translated_title: 看透下一步：多智能体场景中世界模型引导的类人导航
translated_abstract: 在人群密集的场景中选择下一步动作，不仅仅是避开眼前障碍的问题：某个动作可能在局部是可行的，却会让人偏离人行横道走上马路、切入正在过街的行人流，或在狭窄通道中造成拥堵。这些失败模式仅从当前状态是无法察觉的，而要应对它们就需要推理每个候选动作将会引发的后果。世界模型恰好提供了这种能力，即基于动作条件的未来预测，但在每个决策步骤都 rollout 世界模型的代价是可部署的导航系统无法承受的，因此该领域的研究大多以牺牲前瞻性来换取速度。我们认为这是一种错误的二分法。在以人为中心的导航中，世界模型自然的用武之地是在训练阶段，作为一个将前瞻性蒸馏到快速策略中的偏好 oracle，而不是在推理阶段充当在线规划器。我们将一个离散的视觉动作先验与两个任务对齐的（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出将世界模型置于训练阶段作为偏好oracle，把对未来的前瞻性推理蒸馏进一个快速的视觉动作先验策略中，而非在推理时用作在线规划器，从而在不牺牲速度的前提下实现多智能体场景中类人的导航行为。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes placing a world model at training time as a preference oracle that distills foresight into a fast discrete visual action prior policy, rather than using it as an inference-time online planner, enabling human-like navigation in multi-agent scenes without sacrificing speed.
